messages:
incident-bot: Pager: canary-5xx-spike detected in eu-west-1 (route: /v1/generate). 5xx rate 4.8% over 5m, threshold=3% :rotating_light:
maya: oncall maya here, looking at canary metrics now
tom: I see the same - error pattern looks like connection reset / downstream 503s, starting rollback plan
kira: quick question — this canary included new connection pooling change, right? cc @tom
tom: yes, enabled connection pool size=256 flag in release/2026-03. I'm going to flip the feature flag for canary group A to abort
maya: go ahead, please post the flag command output
tom: `curl -X POST https://flags.redwood/api/v1/flags/release-2026-03/abort -d '{"targets":"canary-a"}'`
# flag response: {
#   "status":"ok",
#   "applied":true,
#   "affected_hosts":12
# }
maya: flag flipped :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: automatic action: traffic routing fallback engaged -> route canary A -> fallback model variant (cpu-safe)
ran: I'm scaling the inference pool + increasing max connections on frontdoor, but tail latency still high on a subset of hosts
linda-support: we have 8 customer tickets flagged as "chat timeouts" starting ~10:12 UTC, adding customer-impact tag and priority P1
kira: looking at K/V cache logs — there are spike evictions coincident with canary traffic. suspecting aggressive prefetch + smaller cache size on the new image
tom: given ongoing 5xx and cache anomalies, I'm initiating full rollback to previous stable deployment for roll wave 3 and pausing further rollouts
maya: executing rollback now. executing runbook step: rollback-deploy -> previous-image:v1.9.2
maya: `deployctl rollback --service inference --to-image previous-image:v1.9.2 --wave wave-3`
# deployctl: rollback started, wave-3: 12 hosts -> draining
ran: rolling drain in progress; monitoring 5xx/latency. will also disable prefetch config remotely to reduce eviction pressure
tom: prefetch disabled on canary group A: `configctl set inference.prefetch.enabled false --target canary-a`
linda-support: posting initial customer comms: "We're aware of issues affecting chat timeouts in EU, mitigation underway, ETA 30-45m" — approved by product on duty
maya: creating incident INC-2026-0422 and paging infra/sre/pager duty leads. Adding postmortem template link: https://wiki.redwood/incidents/INC-2026-0422
kira: I've pulled heap and cache metrics; after disabling prefetch, evictions dropped 80% on affected hosts. hypothesis: new pooling + prefetch caused memory pressure -> evictions -> upstream 503s
ran: 5xx rate dropping to 0.9% over 5m after rollback progress and routing fallback. continuing to monitor for 15m window
maya: agreed — if we hold under 1% for 15m, we'll mark customer-impact mitigated and start RCA investigation
tom: leaving note: preserved logs and perf traces at /var/ops/incidents/INC-2026-0422/traces.tar.gz
linda-support: updated tickets with mitigation note and provisional SLA credit language
maya: handing off to night oncall @tom for 15:00-19:00 UTC watch window. if 5xx creeps >1.5% re-page SRE lead. closing active coordination in thread, will update incident doc
tom: ack, i'll watch metrics and follow up on postmortem. thanks all :pray:
summary: Canary triggered 5xx spike in eu-west-1, feature-flagged connection pooling + prefetch suspected. Abort flag flipped, routing fallback engaged, rollback to previous image initiated, prefetch disabled. 5xx reduced below threshold; incident created INC-2026-0422; customer comms and handoff performed.
